preprocessing: PIL RGB; resize 224x224 bilinear antialias; ImageNet normalization
imbalance: training-only sqrt inverse-frequency class weights normalized to mean1
loss_reduction: weighted numerator / target-weight sum across whole effective batch
scheduler: ReduceLROnPlateau; mode=max accuracy; factor=0.5; patience=2; threshold=0; threshold_mode=abs; cooldown=0; min_lr=1e-7
head: GAP; preserve native ConvNeXt normalization; dropout; linear7
question: Does stronger AdamW weight decay improve generalization and the useful ensemble contribution of our proven ConvNeXt-Tiny representation?
early_stopping: Full20-epoch window; no extension. Meaningful cumulative accuracy+.002/F1+.003 counters recorded; raw bests saved independently.
comparability: Historical S06 cohort, ImageNet weights, architecture/head, seed,224,flip,weightedCE,effective32,AdamW/LRs/raw-accuracy LR scheduling are preserved. Planned optimizer intervention: decay0.0001->0.05 on the original parameter groups (including norm/bias). Engineering amendment: guarded FP32 validation instead of historical AMP; this can change selection/scheduler trajectories, so this is not a pure causal weight-decay estimate. Seed/runtime alone do not reproduce the old trajectory.
initialization: Same fresh cached ImageNet1k initialization as S06; full-network fine-tuning, not a resume of an overfit HAM10000 checkpoint
ensemble_plan: After user returns: use the standalone macro-F1 winner for one S83 six-member replacement of original S06 Tiny; original CBAM member retained; equal1/6 unchanged. No weight/checkpoint sweep.
literature_scope: Official ImageNet training defaults AdamW decay0.05; not a HAM10000 result or proof of an optimal fine-tuning setting. Our original group membership is retained rather than copying official norm/bias exclusion or the entire recipe.
